It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where political powers grow cold toward the Gospel and seek to claim authority that belongs to the King alone, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the boundaries of the church’s existence and its right to gather in this hour? [13, 252, 1331, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who use human law as a “scourge” against the faithful, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory where “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [1, 13, 20, 92, 262, 1143, 1283, 1301, 1405, 1425, 1471, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many seek “diplomatic relations” with the culture to avoid the “scars” of the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by reminding us that our “citizenship is in heaven” [11, 15, 19, 21, 26, 28, 38, 41, 132, 1197, 1313, 1316, 1320, 1326, 1426, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the church’s existence is a “divine guarantee” subject only to the “decree from God” who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 68, 121, 201, 258, 676, 1143, 1392, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Sovereign Architect of the Assembly**

**Verse**
“ ‘And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it’ ” (Matthew 16:18). [1084, 1426, Conversation History]. “And He put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all” (Ephesians 1:22–23). [286, 1096, 1431, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that Jesus Christ is the “exclusive and absolute” Master who has “purchased us” by His own blood, meaning the church is His “private property” and not an “administrative anomaly” permitted by the state [203, 304, 320, 1406, 1670, Conversation History]. The “record of history” proves that Christ is the “sovereign architect” who “builds His church” through His own power, for “ ‘of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end, upon the throne of David and over His kingdom’ ” (Isaiah 9:7) [12, 24, 25, 142, 149, 1315, 1406, 1445, 1503, 1617, Conversation History]. Because “ ‘all authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth,’ ” the church’s right to exist and gather is a “binding and authoritative mandate” from the King of Kings, not a “formal license” from a “politician” (Matthew 28:18) [11, 21, 68, 101, 125, 287, 807, 907, 1316, 1432, 1503, 1528, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by “worldly philosophy” that suggests the church is a “social club” dependent on “government registration,” for “your life is not your own” and you belong to a “kingdom which cannot be shaken” (Hebrews 12:28; 1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [12, 101, 113, 212, 858, 1138, 1262, 1341, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word” which declares that “ ‘the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands’ ” (Acts 7:48; Proverbs 28:26) [11, 13, 24, 87, 91, 172, 209, 251, 612, 851, 1039, 1042, 1313, 1381, 1406, 1445, 1503, 1646, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Theocracy to Ekklesia**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, Israel was a “theocratic nation” where “national greatness” and the “temple” were “temporal signs” of favor [409, 718, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” showing that the church is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” (*ekklesia*) who are “sojourners and pilgrims” on the earth, for “Jesus answered, ‘My kingdom is not of this world’ ” (John 18:36; 1 Peter 2:11) [13, 17, 21, 26, 28, 38, 142, 342, 440, 1023, 1113, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1426, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Limit of Civil Authority (Egypt to Rome)**

**Verse**
“ ‘Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God’ ” (Romans 13:1). [75, 895, 1202, 1342, 1473, Conversation History]. “But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the male children alive” (Exodus 1:17). [1211, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—upheld by **Voddie Baucham**—teaches that the state is “ordained by God” as a “minister to you for good” to “punish evildoers,” but its jurisdiction is limited to the “secular arm” and the “physical universe” (Romans 13:4) [15, 18, 20, 29, 75, 1143, 1184, 1284, 1336, 1342, 1422, 1473, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. While we are commanded to “ ‘render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s,’ ” we are simultaneously commanded to give “ ‘to God the things that are God’s,’ ” which include our “worship, teaching, and mercy” (Matthew 22:21) [904, 1024, Conversation History]. When a state like Egypt “afflicts” the people of God with “hard bondage,” it attempts to “write themselves into God’s office,” yet the Lord “dismantles” such powers under His “breathtaking wrath” (Exodus 1:11, 14) [11, 261, 962, 1061, 1118, 1143, 1402, 1502, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our Lawgiver, the LORD is our King; He will save us” (Isaiah 33:22) [94, 201, 948, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You should “lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity” by obeying civil laws in all things that do not violate God’s law, for “this is the will of God” (1 Timothy 2:2; 1 Peter 2:15) [21, 76, 79, 82, 93, 116, 896, 925, 1017, 1105, 1284, 1473, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Divine Decrees**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, God used “hostile nations” as a “rod of My anger” to judge unfaithfulness, as Isaiah wrote: “ ‘Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger and the staff in whose hand is My indignation’ ” (Isaiah 10:5) [717, 740, 763, 859, 924, 1110, 1130, 1133, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “warfare,” teaching that while we “submit yourselves to every ordinance of man,” we must “refuse to yield submission” to any “spirit of fraud” that tries to “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel” (1 Peter 2:13; Galatians 2:5) [11, 15, 19, 75, 1130, 1144, 1246, 1284, 1316, 1342, 1422, 1431, 1473, 1503, 1528, 1532, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Posture of Unwavering Allegiance**

**Verse**
“But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: ‘We ought to obey God rather than men’ ” (Acts 5:29). [48, 1130, 1176, 1205, 1247, 1249, 1256, 1300, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History]. “Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went home. And in his upper room, with his windows open toward Jerusalem, he knelt down on his knees three times that day, and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as was his custom since early days” (Daniel 6:10). [1007, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **Paul Washer**—teaches that the church has an “urgent mandate” to “herald, proclaim, or speak publicly” the Savior, and it must “refuse to yield submission” when the state offers “protection and registration” in exchange for “ecclesiastical jurisdiction” [11, 15, 19, 68, 125, 241, 280, 530, 785, 822, 912, 1130, 1316, 1432, 1503, 1528, 1636, 1638, 1720, Conversation History]. When the Sanhedrin—the “highest religious court in Israel”—was “riddled with injustice” and sought to “silence” the apostles, they established that “cowardice and authentic faith are antithetical” [130, 205, 765, 824, 1069, 1118, 1316, 1422, 1720, Conversation History]. Like Daniel, the believer recognizes that “ ‘His kingdom is one which will not be destroyed,’ ” and therefore, “neither king, nor pope, nor politician” can occupy the office of the church’s Head (Daniel 7:14) [25, 103, 1433, 1503, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict,” knowing that “the Word of God is not chained” (1 Thessalonians 2:2; 2 Timothy 2:9) [11, 25, 41, 51, 76, 91, 123, 767, 1031, 1033, 1081, 1406, 1420, 1431, 1461, 1503, 1504, 1646, 1670, 1720, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” for “your life is not your own” and your “sole objective” is to “testify to the gospel of the grace of God” (1 Corinthians 9:27; Acts 20:24) [11, 12, 13, 27, 31, 79, 101, 116, 130, 323, 782, 843, 861, 975, 1022, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1623, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “testifying in a dispute” required “two or three witnesses” to establish a “legal verdict,” a principle that reflects God’s own “standard of utmost accuracy” in His Word (Deuteronomy 17:6) [330, 584, 1012, 1056, 1072, 1220, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “repose of the soul,” revealing that because “ ‘the kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ,’ ” we find our “rest” in the “finished work” of the Savior rather than in “ritualized ceremonies” (Revelation 11:15; John 19:30) [13, 17, 24, 103, 133, 136, 142, 158, 174, 650, 1199, 1313, 1315, 1445, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Reckoning for Usurpers**

**Verse**
“ ‘And in the days of these kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed; and the kingdom shall not be left to other people; it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever’ ” (Daniel 2:44). [20, 24, 26, 748, 1383, 1493, Conversation History]. “Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 133, 158, 174, 182, 650, 1199, 1315, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of state overreach by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 16, 20, 21, 23, 24, 31, 35, 103, 136, 182, 815, 1113, 1199, 1233, 1259, 1260, 1266, 1268, 1288, 1290, 1300, 1301, 1311, 1315, 1503, 1515, 1519, 1524, 1532, 1636, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. Every ruler who seeks to “write themselves into God’s office” by claiming authority over the church’s worship will ultimately be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27) [11, 15, 26, 30, 37, 324, 412, 914, 1061, 1143, 1402, 1450, 1502, 1720, Conversation History]. On that Day, every human “monument of pride” and “storage city” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away,” but “the Word of our God stands forever” (Isaiah 40:8; Psalm 102:3) [11, 32, 35, 37, 39, 43, 63, 789, 836, 940, 976, 1211, 1233, 1241, 1306, 1315, 1408, 1460, 1515, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Lord knows those who are His” and His “everlasting dominion” is the only kingdom that “shall not pass away” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Timothy 2:19; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 87, 92, 103, 109, 121, 147, 176, 179, 182, 201, 211, 257, 266, 273, 278, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 352, 361, 382, 386, 405, 412, 413, 414, 444, 449, 455, 470, 553, 587, 588, 591, 602, 603, 614, 630, 717, 788, 803, 815, 816, 825, 827, 852, 869, 903, 912, 917, 921, 940, 947, 958, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1183, 1197, 1203, 1206, 1211, 1218, 1233, 1243, 1251, 1252, 1255, 1257, 1259, 1282, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1315, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1441, 1450, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1636, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. Find “tranquility of soul” by “resting upon the surest foundation,” for “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6) [5, 11, 13, 21, 24, 25, 41, 47, 83, 92, 101, 102, 113, 116, 121, 147, 152, 168, 172, 176, 192, 198, 201, 206, 209, 211, 222, 267, 273, 279, 282, 285, 286, 292, 299, 300, 313, 315, 324, 325, 332, 351, 352, 359, 361, 405, 412, 413, 414, 442, 444, 449, 591, 594, 595, 596, 602, 614, 630, 710, 718, 734, 782, 827, 829, 830, 836, 842, 844, 852, 856, 881, 882, 901, 902, 920, 921, 935, 938, 940, 947, 957, 982, 985, 986, 997, 1012, 1016, 1032, 1033, 1035, 1101, 1111, 1113, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1181, 1214, 1221, 1225, 1254, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1315, 1406, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1445, 1450, 1479, 1502, 1503, 1508, 1515, 1572, 1646, 1670, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 291, 297, 300, 311, 324, 325, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 424, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

In fact, the characteristic attitude of all true kingdom citizens is that they are “poor in spirit” (Matt. 5:3). They recognize and confess their own utter spiritual poverty. So Jesus’ final reply to the man, “Go and do likewise,” should have moved the lawyer to plead for grace and forgiveness. If that is what the law means when it promises life to those who obey (Lev. 18:5), we have no hope at all under the law. The only thing the law can do for us is doom us. “The commandment, which was to bring life, [is thus instead] found to bring death” (Rom. 7:10). Because the law demands absolute and utter godlike perfection (Matt. 5:48), no one who has ever sinned can be fit for eternal life on the law’s terms. That’s what the lawyer should have realized. So should we. The full truth is that even Christians, into whose hearts “the love of God has been poured out” (Rom. 5:5), do not consistently love like the law demands.

The Judge The scenario described in the parable would likely be all too familiar to anyone in first-century Israel. Jesus sets the scene in “a certain city” (Luke 18:2) without naming the place. He didn’t need to. Widows and corrupt judges were familiar characters throughout the culture of that time. Justice was often hard to come by. The highest religious court in Israel, of course, was the Great Sanhedrin, consisting of seventy-one judges (all religious leaders deemed experts in both Old Testament law and oral tradition). Their power, as we know from the New Testament, was oppressive and often unjust. Of course, the Great Sanhedrin devised and carried out the conspiracy that led to Jesus’ crucifixion, so we know that body was riddled with injustice and corruption.

But when He was alone, those around Him with the twelve asked Him about the parable. And He said to them, “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those who are outside, all things come in parables, so that ‘Seeing they may see and not perceive, And hearing they may hear and not understand; Lest they should turn, And their sins be forgiven them.’” (Mark 4:10–12) So the short, simple answer to our opening question is that the parables are tools with which Jesus taught and defended the truth.

They water down the gospel, shorten their already shallow sermons, and adapt a market-driven strategy for ministry. In so doing, they rebel against Christ!

To the Colossians, Paul would similarly underscore the all-encompassing implications of Christ’s sovereign lordship: “Whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus” (Col. 3:17), even telling the slaves in that congregation, “Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord” (v. 23). Over and over again, perhaps more than any other theme, Paul’s writings evidence an intimate understanding of the subservient relationship of a believer to Christ—namely, that Jesus is his Master and he is but a slave.

Blaikie noted the integral relationship of these two doctrines, though from the reverse perspective: “The men of those times did not, like so many now, deem it enough to recognize Christ’s headship over themselves personally; they joined to that with all the ardour of their nature, His headship over the whole Church. To repudiate the one was as great a crime and as great a folly as to repudiate the other.
